intro: Six game concepts built from the gaps and trends in this atlas, each with a plan to build, launch and run it. Recommended path: make the top-ranked concept your flagship. If you can't hire a network programmer, start with the couples co-op game instead, because it needs much simpler tech.
caveat: No dataset can guarantee a hit. Most Steam games earn very little, and even acclaimed cozy games have failed commercially (Wanderstop, Venba). These are the best-supported bets in this data. Each one comes with targets and kill criteria, so you learn early and cheaply whether it's working. Scores are research-based judgements; adjust the weights to fit your team.

factors.label: Player demand
factors.description: How strongly players want this, from niche demand scores, comparable sales and player requests.

factors.label: Low competition
factors.description: How uncrowded the niche is (11 minus supply). Higher means fewer direct competitors.

factors.label: Fits a small team
factors.description: How realistic it is for a 3–6 person studio to ship it well within two years.

factors.label: Revenue potential
factors.description: Price point, DLC and expansion headroom, and audience willingness to pay.

factors.label: Easy to market
factors.description: Whether the hook reads in one capsule image or a five-second clip, and appeals to streamers.

factors.label: Trend momentum
factors.description: Whether the underlying trends are rising, peaking or declining.

concepts.name: Driftgarden
concepts.niche: Cozy survival-lite crafting · co-op 1–4 · ocean setting
concepts.oneLiner: Grow a floating garden-boat with up to three friends and sail a flooded, sunlit archipelago. No death, no hunger bars, no rush.
concepts.pitch: The islands have slipped beneath a gentle sea. You and your friends tend a houseboat that is also a garden: plant on the deck, fish over the rail, salvage sunken cottages, and graft new rooms onto the hull as it grows. Each island has a small community to help and a biome to bring back to life. It keeps survival-craft's 'gather, craft, expand, explore' loop, the best-performing niche in the research, removes everything punishing, and is built for co-op from day one.
concepts.audience: Friend groups and couples aged 18–40 who play Stardew, Dinkum or Webfishing together and bounced off Raft or Valheim as too stressful. Also solo cozy players who want exploration beyond a farm.
concepts.sessionLength: 30–90 minutes; one in-game day at sea takes about 20 minutes
concepts.artDirection: Bright stylized 3D with a watercolor sea and chunky, readable silhouettes. The capsule should say 'a garden on a boat' at thumbnail size.

demand.why: Cozy crafting/survival-lite and co-op 2–4 both score demand 9. 28% of open-world survival-craft games reach 1,000 reviews, the best of 23 niches measured.

gap.why: Survival-lite supply is 5 and ocean settings are 3, against farming at 9. Few games combine no-death survival with co-op and the sea.

scopeFit.why: 3D plus online co-op is the hardest scope in this list. Feasible for 5–6 people over about 24 months with peer-to-peer networking and no servers, but it needs a network programmer.

monetization.why: Supports a $19.99 price, friend 4-packs, a supporter pack and paid expansions. Co-op means each sale tends to pull in more sales.

marketability.why: Co-op chaos and boat-building make great clips and streams. 'Garden on a boat' reads instantly.

momentum.why: Co-op keywords and cozy survival-crafting are both rising among successful Steam games; Webfishing and Dinkum show friend-group cozy selling.

whyNow: Cozy crafting/survival-lite is the strongest data-backed gap: demand 9, supply 5, and the niche is filling more slowly than Steam overall.
Co-op for 2–4 is the next clearest gap (demand 9, supply 6). Netcode cost keeps small teams out, which is exactly why it's open.
Ocean settings are rare (supply 3) and players keep asking for cozy games that aren't farming sims.
Webfishing (an estimated 1M+ copies, 97% positive) proved friend-group cozy sells without servers or an MMO-sized burn rate.
pillars: Never punish: no death, no starving, no lost items. Weather sets the mood; it isn't a threat.
Co-op first, solo-friendly: every system works alone and gets better with 2–4 players.
The boat is your home: building and decorating happen on something that travels.
Every island is a small story: help a community, restore a biome, unlock a crop.

mvp: 2-player online co-op over Steam's peer-to-peer networking (no servers to run)
Starter boat with 6 garden plots and 3 craftable rooms
One island with 4 islanders and a restoration quest
60–90 minutes of polished play for the Next Fest demo
launch: Early Access: 1–4 players with drop-in, drop-out co-op
5 islands across 3 biomes, 40 crops, 30 fish, 25+ room modules and free decorating
Controller support and Steam Deck Verified
English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese and German at launch
postLaunch: Free content update every 10–12 weeks: a new island, festival or crop set
1.0 relaunch with the full archipelago and an ending
Paid expansion with a new sea region ($9.99–14.99) 6–9 months after 1.0
Switch 2 and PS5 ports through a porting partner; boat-design share codes

later: Xbox (a Game Pass deal is worth pitching)

pricing.model: Premium with free updates, then a paid expansion
details: Cozy games at $20+ reach 1,000 reviews far more often than cheap ones (45% vs 2.7% under $5).
Friend 4-pack at about 15% off so groups buy together.
10% launch discount, then seasonal sales within Steam's cooldown rules.
Use Valve's recommended regional pricing; China pricing matters.

monetizationPlan: Base game sales are the business: aim for 80%+ of year-one revenue.
Free Early Access updates to drive review count and pull wishlisters back.
$4.99 cosmetic Supporter Pack (sails, hull paint) at launch. Rusty's Retirement saw an 11% attach rate.
Paid expansion ($9.99–14.99) 6–9 months after 1.0, plus soundtrack and artbook DLC.
No microtransactions, gacha or premium currency. Cozy players punish them.
Later: console ports, plush of the boat's mascot, merch once the community is large.

team.note: Owns the vision, systems design and the publisher conversations.
The most important hire. Owns co-op sync from week one.
Farming, fishing, crafting and boat-building systems.
Water shader, characters, the game's look.
From month 3: short video, Discord, festivals, creators.
Composer and sound, localization, QA, console porting.

budgetUSD.label: $0.9–1.6M
budgetUSD.note: Six people for about 24 months, plus contractors, tools, localization and festivals. A 4-person core with a longer Early Access brings it to about $0.6M. The research's derived range for co-op survival-lite with 4–8 devs over 24–30 months is $0.8–2.5M.

Steam page goes live with 'cozy co-op survival' in the first line, GIF-led screenshots and a Simplified Chinese page.

Pitch publishers and porting partners with wishlist data. Prepare the press kit. Reach out to Bilibili and Weibo creators for China.
Early Access launch, timed away from big releases. 10% launch discount and the friend 4-pack.
Each update ships with a trailer, a devlog and a sale.
1.0 relaunch as a second marketing beat: new trailer, press push and showcase slot.

Content update against a public roadmap. Fields of Mistria held 98% positive with this approach.
In-game festivals timed to Steam's seasonal sales.
Community-voted features, boat-design contests, a creator program with keys.
Paid expansion and ports, then fund game two from revenue.

Below about 2k, games see little lift from Next Fest.
About 7k reaches Popular Upcoming; 20k gives a healthy first week.
The median conversion for games over $10.
Cozy hits sit at 92–98%. Players punish jank.
Covers about half of a lean budget in year one; ports and the long tail cover the rest.

killCriteria: The 2-player prototype isn't fun after 3 months: pivot to Lantern Stall, the couples concept.
Fewer than 2,000 wishlists 6 months after the Steam page goes live: change the hook and capsule, or cut scope.
Fewer than 7,000 wishlists after Next Fest: delay Early Access and rework, or ship a smaller single-player version.
Peer-to-peer sync still unstable at month 8: cap co-op at 2 players and ship.

risks.mitigation: Hire the network programmer first, use Steam's peer-to-peer networking, cap at 4 players, no persistent server world.
Playtest with cozy players, not survival fans. Keep the no-fail-state pillar non-negotiable.

risks.risk: Festival slots and attention are crowded
risks.mitigation: A hook that reads at thumbnail size, early applications, wishlists built from short video.

risks.risk: Running out of money before Early Access revenue
risks.mitigation: Marketing or porting-only publisher deal, grants, and burn kept under about $70k a month.
Ship updates fast and own the community.

concepts.revenueAssumptions: Assumes $19.99. Net to studio ≈ $9.80 per unit after discounts, regional pricing, refunds and Steam's 30% (about 49% of list price). Publisher share not deducted.

revenueScenarios.note: Under 1,000 reviews. The studio needs other funding to continue.
About 3,000+ reviews. Recoups half a lean budget in year one; long tail and ports do the rest.
Top-tier cozy outcome, around Coral Island or Sun Haven. Funds game two.

concepts.name: Lantern Stall
concepts.niche: Cozy co-op for couples · non-Western setting · shop sim
concepts.oneLiner: Run a night-market food stall with your partner: one cooks, one shops and serves, and nobody gets yelled at.
concepts.pitch: A two-player co-op game set in an East or Southeast Asian night market. Pick a culture your team knows first-hand. Each evening one player cooks while the other buys ingredients, chats with regulars and decorates the stall. Regulars bring small stories; market families teach you recipes. It has Overcooked's teamwork without the timer stress, the warmth of Venba and Wanderstop, and shop-sim progression. A Friend's Pass lets the second player join free, so every copy sold recruits another player.
concepts.audience: Couples and close friends looking for a gentle game to share. Couples-gaming threads mostly turn up stressful co-op games. Also players who want cozy games set outside pastoral Europe.
concepts.sessionLength: One night at the market takes about 25 minutes, a natural stopping point for an evening session
concepts.artDirection: Warm 2.5D lit by lanterns, steam and neon; food rendered lovingly enough to be the screenshot.

demand.why: Couples co-op scores demand 8, and Reddit couples threads keep asking for it. Food and cooking content performs well on social.

gap.why: Couples supply is 4 and non-Western settings 3, but shop sims are flooding (supply 8, +634% in 2026), which pulls this down.

scopeFit.why: Two players, one location, mostly 2.5D. Remote Play Together covers online play cheaply; true online co-op is optional.

monetization.why: $17.99 premium plus recipe-pack DLC. The Friend's Pass means a lower sale per player but wider reach.

marketability.why: Couple creators, food clips and cultural press angles. The hook reads in one screenshot.

momentum.why: Co-op is rising; non-Western settings get strong press, though shop sims are peaking.

whyNow: Couples co-op is demand 8 and supply 4. Couples threads mostly get It Takes Two and A Way Out, not cozy games.
Non-Western settings are a recognized gap (supply 3) and a strong press hook in a homogeneous market.
Tiny Bookshop (500k+) and Supermarket Simulator (about 1.8M) show the shop loop sells. Co-op and a distinctive theme are what separate the top performers from the flood.
pillars: Two roles, one rhythm: each player has a job that makes the other's matter.
No failing the dinner rush: customers wait patiently, and mistakes become funny moments.
The market is a neighborhood: regulars, families and stories that unfold over weeks.
Authentic food and place, made with people who grew up there.

mvp: Couch co-op plus Steam Remote Play Together
Asymmetric cook and runner roles that can be swapped
A 40-minute demo covering two market nights
launch: Full release: 40 recipes, 25 regulars with story arcs, stall decorating
Solo mode with a helper character
Friend's Pass: the second player plays free
Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean and English at launch
postLaunch: Switch 2 port: couch co-op fits the console

details: Priced near $20, where cozy games reach scale far more often.
A Friend's Pass turns every buyer into a recruiter, as It Takes Two did.

monetizationPlan: Paid recipe packs from new regions ($4.99 each).
Soundtrack DLC; the lantern-lit music suits lofi playlists.
Later: a physical cookbook with real recipes (Stardew's cookbook shows the appetite).

team.note: Co-op design and the economy of a market night.
Gameplay, couch co-op, Remote Play support.
The food has to look delicious.

budgetUSD.label: $350–650k
budgetUSD.note: Four people for about 16 months plus contractors and festivals. No Early Access: a polished premium launch with a Next Fest demo.

milestones.deliverable: One night at the market playable in couch co-op

Next Fest demo; send keys to couples gaming creators.
Launch near Valentine's Day or Lunar New Year.

Paid recipe pack plus a sale.
Valentine's Day and Lunar New Year events and sales.

Shows the game is played as a pair, which is the point.
Recoups the budget in about 18 months.

Fewer than 7,000 wishlists after Next Fest: cut content and ship lean, or push for a showcase slot.

Team members or paid consultants from that culture; credit them visibly.
A solo mode with a helper character.

concepts.revenueAssumptions: Assumes $17.99. Net ≈ $8.80 per unit after discounts, regional pricing, refunds and Steam's 30%. Friend's Pass players are not counted as sales.

concepts.name: Lamplighter's Rest
concepts.oneLiner: Keep a lighthouse inn on a foggy coast and help gentle ghosts finish their unfinished business.
concepts.pitch: Players asked for 'cozy, but with Dredge's mystery'. You run a small inn at the foot of a lighthouse. By day you cook, garden and repair; by night ghosts drift in, each with something left undone. Solving their stories restores the town and the coastline. No fail states, no jump scares, just a soft unease and a lot of warmth. It has a built-in Halloween marketing moment every year.
concepts.audience: Dredge, Spiritfarer and Strange Horticulture fans; cozy players who want more story and a darker edge.
concepts.sessionLength: One day/night cycle takes about 30 minutes
concepts.artDirection: Hand-painted 2D or stylized 3D, fog and lamplight, a muted palette with warm interiors.

demand.why: Spooky cozy demand is 6. Dredge (1M+ in its first year) and Spiritfarer (1M+) show the ceiling.

gap.why: Supply is 4: few games commit to gentle-spooky.

scopeFit.why: Single-player and content-led. Manageable with 4 people in 18 months.

monetization.why: Premium narrative games have less long-tail and DLC headroom than systemic ones.

marketability.why: A seasonal Halloween hook, a strong mood and streamable stories.

momentum.why: Cozy hybrids are rising, but narrative cozy is commercially harder.

whyNow: Players explicitly ask for cozy games with a darker or more mysterious edge (r/GirlGamers, Dredge threads).
Spooky cozy supply is low (4) and Halloween gives a free marketing moment every year.
pillars: Unease, never fear
Every ghost is a short story with a satisfying end
The inn grows as the coast heals
coreLoop: Restore a piece of the coast

mvp: Inn day loop and one ghost story
launch: 20 ghost stories, 5 town areas, inn upgrades

team.note: The ghost stories are the product.

marketingPlan.action: Ghost-story micro-fiction clips; atmospheric GIFs.
Spooky and cozy showcases; Next Fest demo.
Launch in October alongside Halloween sales and coverage.

liveOps.what: New ghost story and Halloween event.

kpis.why: Narrative games depend on the launch spike.
Narrative games live on word of mouth.

killCriteria: Playtesters don't care about the second ghost: rework the writing before building more.

risks.risk: Narrative games are critically loved but sell less
risks.mitigation: Add a systemic inn loop for replay value.
Tone tests with cozy players; no jump scares.

concepts.name: Bloom Harbor (Roblox)
concepts.oneLiner: A free cozy harbor garden on Roblox where friends grow, trade and show off rare plants.
concepts.pitch: Grow a Garden showed idle gardening may be the largest cozy fantasy of any format, peaking at 22M concurrent players. This is a small, fast Roblox experience built around growing, trading and decorating a shared harbor garden. It's a low-cost way to test a cozy loop, reach a huge young audience and build Roblox skills, while the main PC game is in development.
concepts.audience: Roblox players aged 9–16 who play gardening and pet experiences with friends.
concepts.artDirection: Bright Roblox-native style with rare plants that look collectible.

demand.why: Roblox cozy demand is 10. Grow a Garden reached 35B+ visits.

gap.why: Supply is 9. Every Roblox trend is cloned within weeks.

scopeFit.why: Cheap to ship, but it needs live ops, trend speed and Luau skills a PC team may not have.

monetization.why: Game passes and items; top creators earn a lot, the median earns little.

whyNow: Grow a Garden proved the fantasy at enormous scale in 2025.
Roblox paid creators more than $1.5B in 2025.
pillars: Rare plants worth showing off
Trading with friends
Updates every week

postLaunch: Crossover cosmetics with the PC game

details: Avoid pay-to-win; sell cosmetics and convenience.

team.note: Hire or contract people with shipped experiences.

budgetUSD.label: $40–120k
budgetUSD.note: 3–4 months to launch, then weekly updates. Run it as an experiment with a fixed budget.

marketingPlan.action: Roblox sponsored ads in small tests; TikTok clips of rare plants.
Update countdowns; reach out to Roblox YouTubers.

liveOps.what: New seeds or an event every week; Roblox audiences expect it.

kpis.why: Roblox benchmark for a viable experience.
Signals the algorithm is picking it up.

killCriteria: No growth after 8 weeks of updates: stop and keep the lessons.

risks.mitigation: Ship fast and own a distinct look.
Separate contractors and a fixed budget.

concepts.revenueAssumptions: Net is DevEx payout after Roblox's share. 'Units' here means monthly active players at the year-one peak.

revenueScenarios.note: Grow a Garden scale. Extremely rare.

concepts.name: Quilt Porch
concepts.oneLiner: Piece together quilts square by square; each finished quilt tells a family's story.
concepts.pitch: A relaxing tile-placement puzzle built for older players: large readable text, no timers, one-handed controls, generous undo. Each quilt is a puzzle whose patterns score when they match; finishing one unlocks a chapter of the family it belongs to. It's a Dorfromantik-style calm puzzle aimed squarely at the 52M US gamers over 50, who mostly play puzzle games on tablets.
concepts.audience: Players 50+ who play puzzle and word games on tablets and PCs, plus cozy puzzle fans of any age.
concepts.artDirection: Tactile fabric textures, high-contrast patterns, big friendly UI.

demand.why: Older-adult cozy demand is 7; 73% of US gamers over 50 play puzzle games.

gap.why: Supply is 3: almost nobody targets this audience on purpose.

scopeFit.why: 2D, single-player, puzzle content. Three people in about 12 months.

monetization.why: This audience spends less and plays mostly on mobile.

marketability.why: Hard to reach through Steam and gaming creators; needs Facebook and craft communities.

momentum.why: A steady market, not a rising trend.

whyNow: 52.4M US gamers are 50+ and 73% of them play puzzle games.
Accessibility for older players is a recurring request with almost no targeted supply.
pillars: Readable at arm's length
Never rushed
Every quilt is a memory

launch: 40 quilts, a daily quilt mode, family story chapters
postLaunch: A real-world quilting pattern book tie-in

details: No ads or energy systems; this audience hates them.

monetizationPlan: Pitch Apple Arcade for an upfront deal

marketingPlan.action: Quilting and craft communities, Facebook groups, AARP-style outlets, puzzle newsletters.
Mother's Day or holiday timing; gift-friendly pricing.

liveOps.what: A new quilt pack each season.

killCriteria: Older testers find it confusing after two UI iterations: rethink the core puzzle.

risks.mitigation: Marketing through craft communities and partners, not gaming press.
Keep the budget small; pitch Apple Arcade.

concepts.revenueAssumptions: Blended net ≈ $5.50 per unit across PC ($12.99) and mobile ($6.99) after store fees and discounts.

concepts.name: Sill
concepts.oneLiner: A tiny window-box garden that grows along the bottom of your screen while you work, and your friends' plants can visit.
concepts.pitch: A small studio launchpad. Desktop idle games spread fast (Rusty's Retirement sold 330k+ copies on Steam at $7; Bongo Cat peaked at 194k concurrent players). Sill is a window box that sits at the bottom of the screen, grows while you work, and lets friends' plants pollinate yours. It's 4–6 months for two people. The goal is cash flow, Steam followers and a mailing list to launch the flagship to, not a fortune.
concepts.audience: People who work at a PC and want something gentle on screen: students, writers, remote workers.
concepts.sessionLength: Runs for hours in the background, with short check-ins
concepts.artDirection: Crisp pixel or vector plants that look good at 120px tall.

demand.why: Idle/desktop demand is 7 and players explicitly ask for 'something cozy to run while working'.

gap.why: Supply is 10: idle releases are up 150% in 2026.

marketability.why: Desktop screenshots and streamer overlays spread well.

momentum.why: The format is now flooding; the early hits have already happened.

whyNow: Rusty's Retirement shows the format can fund a solo developer.
A cheap, fast first release builds the audience the flagship launches to.
pillars: Never in the way
Something new every time you glance down
Friends make it better

details: Idle games do best between $10 and $14.99 for reaching 1,000 reviews; $7.99 is an impulse-buy compromise.

milestones.gate: Testers keep it open for a full workday

marketingPlan.action: Desktop clips, 'what's on my screen' posts, the Idle Fest on Steam.
Twitch overlay angle for streamers.

kpis.why: Enough to make a cheap game profitable.

risks.mitigation: The friends feature is the differentiator; keep scope tiny.
